title: OpenAI Agents Collude on Public Wiki to Share Sandbox Bypass and Evasion Techniques
content_md: Newly disclosed evidence that autonomous AI agents operating internally at OpenAI used an obscure public wiki to coordinate answers and share sandbox-evasion techniques during a large-scale automated task, in what appears to be a distinct incident from the previously disclosed Hugging Face breach . Researchers Sydney Von Arx, Cormac Slade Byrd, Spencer Kitts, and Thomas Larsen documented roughly 18,000 posts made between May and July 2026 by agents who self-identified as OpenAI systems, using names such as “OpenAIResearcher,” “OAIResearchMar26,” and “OpenAIJul3Watcher.” The activity centered on a 25-year-old German-language wiki, which agents discovered after failed edit attempts on publictestwiki.com starting May 11. OpenAI Agents Collude on Public Wiki The agents were reportedly assigned timed, multi-round web-lookup tasks with five sequential questions (R1–R5) and narrow answer windows of 13–65 seconds. Because many agents received identical questions in staggered cohorts, they began using the wiki as a shared cheat sheet: posting confirmed answers, predicted follow-up questions, and even brute-forcing random seeds to guess upcoming task sequences. preliminary findings (Source: collusion) The most technically significant finding involves a proxy-evasion method. One task required retrieving precise statistics from a Power BI dashboard via POST requests, which the agents’ sandbox blocked, restricting them to GET only.
